note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Dry, persistent cough for 5–6 days.
  - Runny nose. No specific trigger or exposure reported.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset ~5–6 days ago with cough and rhinorrhea; diarrhea at onset resolved after a short period; cough persists and disturbs sleep.
  - Reports chills/shivering; has not measured temperature.
  - Generalized myalgias and lethargy/weakness.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat: sore/irritated from coughing; no pain with swallowing beyond irritation; no reported dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling, or voice change.
  - Nose: runny nose.
  - Ears: no pain, blockage, or discharge.
  - Airway/respiratory: no baseline dyspnea; feels labored only during coughing fits; no chest pain reported; no stridor/noisy breathing mentioned.
  - No facial, lip, tongue, or uvular swelling reported.
  - Neck: no symptoms reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar severe episodes, ED visits, or injection therapies mentioned.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: No known drug allergies.
  - Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context:
  - Lives with partner (partner well).
  - Works in IT; went to work despite symptoms; advised considering time off.
  - Former smoker; quit ~6 months ago.
  - Alcohol: wine ~2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: None reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: Dry cough audible to clinician; patient reports no day-to-day breathlessness; labored breathing only during coughing.
- Mental status and associated features: Reports lethargy/weakness; no dizziness or syncope mentioned.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not recorded.

Assessment:
- Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection with dry cough and rhinorrhea, associated with chills, myalgias, and fatigue.
- Justification: Acute onset (5–6 days), dry cough with nocturnal disturbance, runny nose, systemic symptoms (chills, myalgias), absence of chest pain or persistent dyspnea, and no focal ENT red flags (no dysphagia, drooling, stridor, ear symptoms).
- Comorbidities: Type 2 diabetes and hypertension (on metformin and lisinopril).

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  - Rest and maintain good hydration.
  - Take regular acetaminophen (paracetamol) for symptom relief (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Consider taking 1–2 days off work to rest; reassess returning early next week.
- Follow-up instructions:
  - If not improving in 2–3 days, return for reassessment; if still feeling feverish and cough not improving, clinician may consider antibiotics.
  - Return sooner if breathing is getting worse.
- Escalation criteria/red flags discussed:
  - Worsening breathing.
  - Cough not improving and persistent feverishness.
- Additional counseling:
  - Alcohol reduction suggested (cut down to two glasses per week initially, then consider further reduction), in context of hypertension/diabetes management.
- Emergency contact instructions:
  - None provided in transcript.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals (temperature, pulse, BP, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - No physical ENT exam or chest exam findings documented.
  - No COVID-19 or influenza testing status documented.
  - No medication doses/routes/frequencies documented.
  - No documentation of OTC cough remedies tried.
  - No vaccination status relevant to respiratory infections.
- Internal conflicts:
  - None noted (patient likely meant “breathless” when saying “restless”; no direct conflict).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; some pauses/inaudible segments and minor conversational overlaps, but clinical content sufficient.
